TASK: Author the shipped regression guard BEFORE any retirement work, so it is falsified against the real disease rather than a decoy. Create scripts/verify_retirement.py exposing `scan(root: Path) -> list[Violation]` where Violation is a NamedTuple(leg, path, line, detail), sorted deterministically. It MUST return a list of named legs — never a bool and never a bare exit code — because the per-leg red-proofs must be able to assert `== [LEG_X]`. A CLI wrapper exits 1 on any violation. Enumerate surfaces from `git ls-files`, NOT Path.rglob, so a file deleted from the working tree but still in the index is still seen.

FOUR LEGS ONLY (the plan's original eight were cut to four by the cold panel; do not re-add the dropped ones):
  LEG A `retired-path-still-tracked` — `git ls-files` must not list .agent-work/LESSONS.md, .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md, scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py, scripts/verify_lessons_applied.py, scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py. Path-based, so it cannot be paraphrased around. This is the ONLY leg that catches a future agent re-committing LESSONS.md verbatim — that file advertises its own read path in its own preamble, so zero new mentions would appear anywhere else.
  LEG B `unapproved-store-mention` — a frozen approval census. Enumerate every line on the shipped surface naming `episodes/`, `episode store`, `query_episodes`, or `apply_episode_delta`, excluding the store's own module and its own spec, and compare against tests/data/store_mentions.approved.txt (`path:normalized-line` plus a REQUIRED one-line reason per entry). Its failure message must state the discriminator verbatim: 'a new shipped site now names the episode store: <path>:<line>. If this is a WRITE path, approve it with a reason. If it tells an agent to READ the store and condition behaviour on it, it violates constraint:episodes-are-not-prescriptions.' Seed the approved file with the 18 sites that exist today.
  LEG C `replacement-absent` — the PRESENCE half. tests/test_prose_deletions.py's docstring states the rule: 'An absence-only suite would pass just as happily on a template that had deleted everything.' Assert the capture command is named in BOTH spine imperatives, is in the commander AND admiral install bundles, and exists on disk. At g1 this leg is legitimately RED and stays red until g3.
  LEG D `retired-name-on-shipped-surface` — retired names absent from the shipped surface. Each record-only root carries a REQUIRED non-empty reason string: docs/superpowers/ ('historical plans and drills — records, not instructions'), tests/fixtures/ ('recorded transcripts; editing them falsifies a recording'), .agent-work/ ('run records'), episodes/ ('the store itself').

Then tests/test_retirement_guard.py: one decoy red-proof per leg, each building a minimal git repo in tmp_path with EXACTLY ONE planted violation and asserting both `[v.leg for v in scan(decoy)] == [LEG_X]` AND the offending path — so a leg firing for the wrong reason is caught. Plus `test_every_leg_has_a_red_proof` asserting set(LEGS) == set(_REGISTERED) against a leg roster held independently in the test module, so a leg added later without a decoy, or quietly deleted, fails. Plus `test_canon_is_clean` asserting scan(REPO_ROOT) == [], carrying @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason='#447 g6 removes this marker'): the suite stays green while the tree is deliberately dirty, and strict XPASS fails the suite the moment the tree goes clean, so the scaffolding cannot outlive the work.

TASK: Build the write-path replacement BEFORE the old one is removed. Create scripts/verify_episode_captured.py: `verify_episode_captured.py <work-id> [--store-root PATH] [--phase feedback|archive]`. It globs the store's active/ directory for episodes whose mechanical `- run:` line matches the work id, and exits 1 if none. Under --phase archive it additionally requires `git ls-files --error-unmatch` to succeed on each matched path, so a run that writes an episode and forgets to `git add episodes/` genuinely fails.

THE VALVE — this is the load-bearing design property, not a detail. The verifier parses ONLY the `<!-- episode-state: -->` header and the `- run:` line. It MUST NOT parse or emit any assertion `statement`, and MUST NOT import query_episodes. Ids and counts out; statements never. It asserts CAPTURE ONLY — no ripeness, no apply-or-defer, no dormancy; those are playbook concepts that retire with the playbook (decision:capture-gate-checks-capture-only). Prove the valve with a sentinel test: seed a temp store where every statement is 'SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK-9f2a', run the verifier with stdout+stderr captured, assert the sentinel appears in NEITHER; and give that test its own red proof by monkeypatching the verifier to echo the record body and asserting the sentinel IS then found.

STORE ROOT: do NOT change store_root()'s semantics. Its docstring already rules out durable_root() for a documented reason and this retirement is not the place to overturn that ruling. Instead the spine commands pass --store-root explicitly (wired in g3). Verify and record the reason: the installed writer's store_root() resolves to the SKILL INSTALL DIR (~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes), not the project repo — leave a comment at store_root() naming this hazard and pointing at the --store-root requirement.
